diagnostic_evidence.quote: there exists $\sigma<\sigma_2$ such that for any $\phi^0\in\mathcal{B}_{\sigma}(\mathcal{S})$ and some $\widetilde{\phi}_g\in\mathcal{S}$, we have
This means that $\left\{\phi^n\right\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is a Cauchy sequence, and is convergent.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem asserts that a single $\phi_g\in\mathcal{S}$ works for every initial point in a neighborhood of the whole orbit $\mathcal{S}$. Since $\mathcal{S}$ contains a continuum of minimizers (phase shifts and rotations), an initial point near a different orbit point converges to that different point, not to the fixed $\phi_g$. The proof only shows that for each $\phi^0$ there is a nearby point $\widetilde{\phi}_g\in\mathcal{S}$ and the sequence converges to some limit, not that the limit is the same fixed $\phi_g$ for all $\phi^0$.

failure_location.quote: there exist $\sigma>0$ and $\phi_g \in \mathcal{S}$ such that for all $\phi^0 \in \mathcal{B}_{\sigma}(\mathcal{S})$, the sequence $\{\phi^n\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ generated by the P-RG has a locally linear convergence rate

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $\mathcal{B}_{\sigma}(\mathcal{S})$ by $\mathcal{B}_{\sigma}(\phi_g)$ for a fixed $\phi_g$, or state that for each $\phi^0\in\mathcal{B}_{\sigma}(\mathcal{S})$ there exists $\phi_g\in\mathcal{S}$ (depending on $\phi^0$) such that the bound holds; update Var-P-convergence and E-eq-Phi accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The local convergence statements and the energy-wavefunction equivalence corollary are not valid as stated for all $\phi^0\in\mathcal{B}_{\sigma}(\mathcal{S})$; they require either fixing the neighborhood around a particular $\phi_g$ or allowing $\phi_g$ to depend on $\phi^0$. The rate estimate itself is unaffected.
issues.title: Local convergence theorems fix a single limit point for initial data near the entire symmetry orbit
issues.why_classification: The main linear rate survives, but the central quantifier/scope of the local convergence is wrong and must be weakened from a uniform statement over the orbit to a pointwise or fixed-point statement.

issues.failure_explanation: The formal theorem gives a linear convergence bound with a fixed contraction factor $(L-\mu)/(L+\mu)+\varepsilon$ for each fixed $\sigma_0$. Decreasing $\sigma_0$ can make this factor arbitrarily small, but for each fixed algorithm it remains a constant less than one; the bound does not show that the contraction factor tends to zero as $n\to\infty$, which is what superlinear convergence would require.

failure_location.quote: Furthermore,  reducing $\sigma_0$ appropriately, one can achieve a P-RG with superlinear local  convergence rate.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace "superlinear local convergence rate" with "linear convergence with an arbitrarily small contraction factor" (or state that the factor tends to zero as $\sigma_0\to0$).
issues.overall_effect: Misleadingly advertises superlinear convergence; the proven guarantee is only linear convergence with an arbitrarily small (but fixed) rate factor.
issues.title: Conclusion claims superlinear convergence from a linear rate with adjustable constant
issues.why_classification: The correction is a short prose change and does not affect the formal theorems or their rates; it only removes an unsupported characterization of the convergence type.
